summary: Interview Prep crash-on-scroll bug fix VERIFIED. Logged in as refactor_test@example.com, navigated to /interview-prep, filled the form (Senior Product Manager @ Stripe + JD), clicked Generate, waited ~47s for the streaming AI response (~14,956 chars) to complete, and then aggressively wheel-scrolled the ScrollArea viewport (scrollTop reached 4000px). design_issues.screen: Interview Prep - Section 7 (Questions To Ask The Interviewer)
issues: The ListBlock rendered an EMPTY <ol> for section 7 in this run (the visible card was blank). Section header parsed correctly and box container rendered, but no list items appeared. Root cause is likely AI output format for section 7 not matching the '/^(\d+)\.\s+(.*)/' numbered-list regex in InterviewPrepRenderer.jsx line 145 (e.g., model may emit '- ' bullets instead of '1. '). Section 6 (Interview Tips) rendered 8 numbered items correctly, so the ListBlock itself works. Consider extending the LIST section parser to also accept '- ' / '* ' bullets, OR tighten the AI prompt to force '1./2./3.' format for section 7.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Interview Prep P0 crash-on-scroll is FIXED. Renderer correctly handles the new structured markdown. Only remaining nit is section 7 sometimes rendering an empty <ol> when the AI emits '-' instead of '1.' bullets — a robustness enhancement, not a blocker. Streaming takes ~40-50s to complete. ScrollArea viewport selector: [data-radix-scroll-area-viewport]. Use page.mouse.wheel() over the element, or el.scrollTo(0, el.scrollHeight) to test scrolling.
rca of the issue: Original crash: the previous renderer parsed sections >=4 as list-only, but the new AI prompt puts Q&A structure (with .difficulty, .followups[], .approach[], .sample[]) in sections 4 & 5. Accessing .map on undefined arrays during mid-stream renders caused 'Cannot read properties of undefined' inside ScrollArea's virtualized re-render on scroll. Fix (already applied by main agent): new parsePrepDocument returns fully-initialized QAItem objects (all arrays default to []) and sectionKindFor(number) routes 2-5 to QA and 6-7 to LIST. Verified: no undefined errors during aggressive scrolling of a 15k-char rendered document.
